subject: GDPR: DPA & SCC selection — controller/processor alignment (AcmeHealth)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call: GDPR DPA / SCC selection — next steps

Hi Sofia — thanks again for a great call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with AcmeHealth's GDPR and procurement needs:

Summary of our call:
- AcmeHealth will be Controller; Redwood Inference will act as Processor for hosted API requests.
- You requested our DPA template and confirmation of which SCC module we intend to sign.
- You also asked for evidence (SOC 2 Type II summary) and to kick off your vendor security questionnaire.

Proposed next steps:
1) I attached our DPA template and a one-page SOC 2 Type II summary (see attachments). Please share with legal/security and let us know any redlines.
2) For SCCs, our standard position is to execute the EU SCCs Module Two (Controller → Processor). If your legal team prefers a different module or needs a processor-to-processor flow, flag that and we can discuss.
3) We'll schedule a short follow-up with Rishi (security lead) to walk through the questionnaire and any technical evidence (logs, retention, encryption).

Can you confirm who on your side should be included in the security questionnaire thread (name + email)? If possible, can we aim to have legal feedback on the DPA by the end of next week?

Thanks — I can set up the follow-up for Tuesday or Wednesday next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.docx, Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf

From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: GDPR DPA / SCC selection — next steps

Thanks Marissa — that recap is helpful. A few quick items from AcmeHealth's side:

- Confirming: AcmeHealth will be Controller. Our legal team typically requests Module Two (Controller → Processor) SCCs, but they'll review.
- Could you confirm whether Redwood will act as Processor only for hosted API (Redwood-hosted inference) or also for Dedicated/Private deployments if we use those options? We need clarity on scope in the DPA.
- Please also confirm whether Redwood is willing to sign a BAA — we have a subset of PHI workflows and may require HIPAA coverage for certain patients data. If you could flag HIPAA readiness, that'll help legal triage.
- For the security questionnaire, please add our security lead: Daniel Price <daniel.price@acmehealth.com> and our procurement contact: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acmehealth.com>.

Acme Legal will start an initial review but will likely request a few redlines around data retention and subprocessors.

Thanks — looking forward to the follow-up.

Best,
Sofia Martinez
Head of Product (AI)
AcmeHealth
sofia@acmehealth.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@acmehealth.com>, Daniel Price <daniel.price@acmehealth.com>, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: GDPR DPA / SCC selection — next steps

Hi Sofia, Daniel, Maria — thanks for looping us in. Quick answers and what we'll provide next:

Scope and role alignment:
- Redwood will act as Processor for hosted API (Redwood-hosted) and for Dedicated capacity where Redwood manages the inference runtime. For Private/on-prem deployments where the customer manages the stack, Redwood's control plane is optional and responsibilities shift — we'll annotate those scopes in the DPA. We'll include a clear definition of "Processing Services" in the DPA to reflect both hosted and dedicated options and a separation for private/on-prem deployments.

SCC module:
- We typically execute EU SCCs Module Two (Controller → Processor) for customer-controller, Redwood-processor relationships. We'll mark Module Two in the proposed DPA and add a note about subprocessors and subprocessors' locations.

HIPAA / BAA:
- Redwood supports HIPAA workloads on Dedicated and Private deployments. We can provide a BAA for customers requiring it; that will be a separate attachment/addendum. For hosted, we support HIPAA under a BAA with specific committed controls — we'll surface the conditions in the BAA draft.

Evidence / attachments:
- Attached: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf (summary), Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.docx (draft DPA with Module Two selected).
- I'll also upload a more detailed SOC 2 package to a secure drive if AcmeLegal requests it.

Security questionnaire and next steps:
- Marissa will send a calendar invite for a 30-min session next week to walk through the questionnaire and provide technical evidence (encryption at rest/in transit, key management, retention, delete workflows, audit logs).
- Action items for AcmeHealth: share legal redlines against the attached DPA and confirm whether a BAA is required for your use case.

If anyone wants to review the DPA inline, I can join with our legal operations lead.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security & Compliance (Redwood Inference)
rishi@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf, Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.docx
